title: KV-prefetch and elastic token-capacity to reduce rerank p99 latency
creator: Marco Del Rey
description: Problem: Our reranking endpoint exhibits tail latency spikes (p99) under mixed load when long queries mix with short ones. Observed causes: oversized microbatches waiting for long-token requests, cold KV-cache misses when reranker tries to rehydrate candidate embeddings, and wall-clock timeouts that cancel useful parallel work. Goal: reduce p99 latency by 30% and p95 by 10% for the rerank endpoint without regressing throughput or quality. Approach: implement KV-prefetch for candidate embeddings on request receipt, introduce an elastic per-worker token capacity limit that prioritizes short queries, and add adaptive microbatch early-flush timeouts tuned by live sequence-length histograms.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% in canary traffic compared to baseline (measured over 24h)
0% regression in rerank relevance (NDCG@10) against the canonical eval set within 48h of rollout
No increase in 95th-percentile GPU utilization beyond 5 percentage points
Feature gated and opt-in by client config; all changes reversible by rollout flag
metrics_baseline: Baseline (2026-02-10): rerank p50=32ms, p95=210ms, p99=760ms (mixed short+long workload)
Baseline throughput: 850 QPS sustained on dedicated pool alpha-12
implementation_notes: KV-prefetch: on request enqueue, kick off async fetch of candidate embeddings using a 'soft' prefetch priority; store in per-request KV slot to avoid duplicate fetches at microbatch time

Elastic token capacity: per-worker token_budget variable that is consumed by inflight requests; short requests (< 64 tokens) marked high-priority and can borrow budget with bounded debt; long requests queued to secondary token pool

Adaptive early-flush: microbatcher monitors sequence-length histogram and dynamically sets an early-flush timeout to trade latency vs batching efficiency (initial policy: 20th percentile -> 5ms, 50th->12ms, 80th->25ms)
Timeout changes: replace rigid per-request generation deadline with cooperative cancellation token to allow partial-kv results to be returned when beneficial
Instrumentation: add per-request KV hit/miss counters, token_budget utilization metrics, and microbatch flush_reason tagging in tracing
risk_and_tradeoffs: Prefetch increases memory pressure and additional egress calls for embeddings; mitigated by bounded prefetch concurrency and TTL on prefetched entries
Elastic token capacity can reduce throughput for large-batch workloads; we will gate by client tier and provide a config knob
Aggressive early-flush reduces batching efficiency and increases cost-per-token; tune via canary and dynamic thresholds
Partial results on cooperative cancellation require client SDK compatibility and clear contract in API docs
testing_plan: Unit tests for KV-prefetch paths and failure/fallback scenarios
Synthetic load tests: mix of short (<=32 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) requests at varying ratios (10/90, 50/50, 90/10)
Chaos tests: simulate KV store latency spikes and worker OOM to verify graceful fallback to on-demand fetch
A/B canary for 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic with automated rollback on latency or quality regressions
Offline eval: NDCG@10 and MRR on canonical rerank testset and adversarial prompt set
rollout_plan: Canary stage 1: internal infra + low-impact customers (1% traffic) for 48h
Canary stage 2: 5% customer traffic for 72h with extended monitoring
Gradual ramp to 20% then 50% over a week if metrics stable
Full rollout gated by monitoring and SRE sign-off; rollback plan pre-prepared (flip flag to old microbatcher)
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: rerank_latency_v2 comparison panel (p50/p95/p99), microbatch efficiency (tokens_per_batch), KV hit rate
Alerts: p99 increases >20% for 30m, KV hit rate drops below 60% for 10m, token_budget starvation rate >1%
Tracing: add tag 'prefetch=true/false' and 'flush_reason' to distributed traces to filter regressions
SLOs impacted: rerank p99 SLO currently 1s; we aim to reduce to 700ms in runtime-1.22
